paper.title: Ace-Skill: Bootstrapping Multimodal Agents with Prioritized and Clustered Evolution
paper.central_claim: Jointly optimizing rollout allocation (a prioritized sampler with lazy-decay proficiency tracking) and knowledge organization (cluster-isolated tactical-experience and strategic-skill pools) breaks a self-reinforcing 'data inefficiency / knowledge interference' loop, giving +35.46% relative Avg@4 over vanilla tool use, letting a 35B MoE match or beat proprietary models, and transferring zero-shot to 9B/4B models.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: no run receipt is exposed to the worker; model_type is the claude-kimi configured type.

materials.notes: Figure panels (Fig. 3-5) are caption/prose only in the text material; no appendix present in the HTML; no page images.

evidence.quote: a co-evolutionary framework that jointly optimizes rollout allocation and knowledge organization for self-evolving multimodal agents
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: two non-weight components (sampling schedule, knowledge organization) are changed.

evidence.quote: data inefficiency, where costly rollout effort is disproportionately spent on low-value samples rather than informative ones, and knowledge interference, where heterogeneous knowledge stored in shared repositories leads to noisy retrieval and task-misaligned guidance
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated bottlenecks.

evidence.quote: Together, these issues form a self-reinforcing failure loop in which uninformative rollouts yield noisy knowledge, which in turn degrades subsequent rollouts.
evidence.support_explanation: Coupling hypothesis; stated, not separately measured.

evidence.quote: As bootstrapping proceeds, the agent’s capability is inherently non-stationary: a sample that is difficult early on may later become routine.
evidence.support_explanation: Rationale for lazy-decay Beta proficiency tracking.

evidence.quote: an exploration floor that prevents starvation and preserves broad coverage
evidence.support_explanation: Sampling weight = uncertainty + hardness + exploration (Eq. 4).

evidence.quote: the cluster structure can be specified a priori rather than adapted online
evidence.support_explanation: Clusters are fixed K-means groups of task-description embeddings; K is a free parameter.

evidence.quote: and its retrieved neighbors are consolidated into a single entry via LLM-based merging
evidence.support_explanation: Entries are inserted or merged by similarity threshold; no outcome-based admission test.

evidence.quote: we further apply a compaction step that iteratively merges the most similar pair until the pool size falls within the budget
evidence.support_explanation: Capacity bound by merging, not by utility-based retirement.

evidence.quote: which is integrated into the current skill document and compressed to satisfy a budget
evidence.support_explanation: Skill document is rewritten (merge + compress) after each rollout; no versioning or rollback.

evidence.quote: the same MLLM serves as the reasoning agent, trajectory summarizer, experience & skill merger, and verifier, all operating in no-thinking mode
evidence.support_explanation: Same model proposes, merges and verifies; no independent referee.

evidence.quote: Training runs for 50 steps with batch size 8, where each sample undergoes 1 rollout of up to 10 agentic turns for TIR-Bench and 20 for other benchmarks
evidence.support_explanation: Bootstrapping budget; train/test split and number of clusters K are not stated anywhere in the text.

evidence.quote: for models smaller than 9B, we adopt Qwen3.5-9B as the verifier, as sub-9B models exhibit hallucinated judgments when serving as a verifier
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier is an LLM whose imperfection is acknowledged.

evidence.quote: “∗” indicates that the results are sourced from (Jiang et al., 2026a), and the others are reproduced using official checkpoints or APIs.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines mix sourced and reproduced numbers.
Store-off baseline: same tools, no bootstrapped knowledge (per-benchmark Avg@4/Pass@4 then mean).
Nearest prior method (XSkill) on the same backbone and tools.
Headline result; single bootstrapping run.

evidence.quote: Ace-Skill with an open-source 35B backbone surpasses GPT-5-mini (+10.79 Avg@4), Gemini-2.5-Pro (+7.53 Avg@4), and even the Qwen3.5-Plus API (+2.89 Avg@4) under the Vanilla Tools setting
evidence.support_explanation: Comparison to proprietary models that receive no bootstrapped knowledge.

evidence.quote: We directly inject the knowledge bootstrapped by Qwen3.5-35B-A3B into the smaller Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-4B at inference time.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-scale reuse of the retained memory.
9B with transferred knowledge vs vanilla mean 17.12 / 33.76.

evidence.quote: We inject experiences and skills bootstrapped exclusively on VisualToolBench into TIR-Bench, and those from MMSearch-Plus into AgentVista.
evidence.support_explanation: Only held-out-source evidence; implies bootstrapping normally uses each benchmark's own samples.

evidence.quote: On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, OOD transfer lifts TIR-Bench Avg@4 from 39.37 to 45.50 (+6.13) and AgentVista from 15.37 to 18.58 (+3.21).
evidence.support_explanation: Positive OOD deltas over store-off, two source-target pairs, single run.

evidence.quote: Per-sample selection frequency of the Prioritized Evolution Sampler over 4 epochs on four benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Sampler runs over each benchmark's own sample pool (4 epochs), so the training pool coincides with benchmark samples.

evidence.quote: This shows that the sampler successfully reallocates compute from easy samples to the ones that matter most.
evidence.support_explanation: Evidence is a visitation histogram, not a sample-efficiency or learning-curve comparison.

evidence.quote: The Prioritized Sampler alone lifts the baseline from 39.37 to 46.25 Avg@4. The Clustered Organizer alone reaches 45.75.
evidence.support_explanation: 2x2 module ablation on TIR-Bench only (full = 50.00).

evidence.quote: yields super-additive improvement on both scales
evidence.support_explanation: Contradicted by own numbers: gains +6.88 and +6.38 individually (sum 13.26) vs +10.63 combined.

evidence.quote: w/o Base Exploration 48.88 52.00 w/o Difficulty Bias 47.50 51.25 w/o Skill Cluster 46.75 51.62 w/o Experience Cluster 48.25 53.00
evidence.support_explanation: Component ablations on TIR-Bench, differences of 1-3 points, single run; on 122B 'w/o Experience Cluster' (53.00) is nearly equal to full 53.12.

evidence.quote: Hyperparameter sensitivity on TIR-Bench (Avg@4).
evidence.support_explanation: rho and gamma were tuned on TIR-Bench, which is also a headline test benchmark.

evidence.quote: the non-clustered system draws eight experiences from the global pool
evidence.support_explanation: Single qualitative maze example showing cross-type noise; no aggregate retrieval-purity measure.

evidence.quote: the overall sample complexity and training time are already significantly reduced compared to standard uniform sampling baselines
evidence.support_explanation: Efficiency claim without reported measurement.

evidence.quote: the online inference cost remains identical to or even lower than the base model due to more accurate, zero-shot tool invocations
evidence.support_explanation: Inference-cost claim without numbers; retrieval + full skill document injected per task.

evidence.quote: these methods typically aggregate all knowledge into a single global pool, incurring cross-type retrieval noise as sample diversity grows, and most operate at a single granularity (either experiences or skills).
evidence.support_explanation: Author's gap statement vs prior skill/experience bootstrapping.

evidence.quote: introduces a dual-stream framework that jointly accumulates experiences and skills through visually grounded summarization
evidence.support_explanation: The closest prior method (XSkill) is already dual-granularity, weakening the 'single granularity' part of the gap.

evidence.quote: Ace-Skill achieves a mean Avg@4 of 31.40 and Pass@4 of 48.23, improving over the Vanilla Tools baseline by +8.22 and +6.91 points, respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline numbers (relative +35.46% Avg@4).

signatures.object: Rollout-allocation schedule over the bootstrapping pool (per-sample proficiency state v_i with lazy-decayed Beta posterior); baseline = sequential/uniform traversal.
signatures.information: Scalar reward r in [0,1] from an LLM verifier (same MLLM; ground-truth answers are part of the training pool); no test labels at inference.
signatures.operation: Update decayed (alpha, beta) per revisited sample -> weight = sqrt(v(1-v)) + gamma(1-v) + eps -> draw batch of 8.
signatures.output: Next batch of samples for rollout and distillation.
signatures.conditions: rho=0.95, gamma=0.4, eps=0.1, 50 steps, 1 rollout per sample.
signatures.selection_rule: Stochastic priority sampling (uncertainty + hardness + exploration floor).
signatures.selection_data: The same pool the memory is built from; whether it overlaps the evaluated benchmark samples is not stated.
signatures.persistence: Proficiency vector exists only during bootstrapping; the persisted result is the memory it fed.
signatures.later_use: Controls which trajectories get distilled into the memory.
signatures.claimed_effect: Sampler alone: TIR-Bench Avg@4 39.37 -> 46.25; >30% of samples visited >4 times and >39% <4 times over 4 epochs.
signatures.failure_boundary: Excess difficulty bias hurts coverage (Fig 5); no learning-curve vs uniform at equal rollouts; single-rollout reward is noisy.

signatures.object: Cluster-isolated knowledge memory: per cluster a tactical experience pool (<=120 entries, similarity-merge threshold 0.70) and a strategic skill document (<= about 1000 words); baseline = single global pool as in XSkill.
signatures.information: Trajectory + verifier reward; distillation by the same MLLM; cluster routing from text embedding of the task description (K-means, fixed a priori).
signatures.operation: Distill delta experience and delta skill after each rollout -> route to the sample's cluster -> insert or LLM-merge by similarity -> compact/compress to caps.
signatures.conditions: K (cluster count) not reported; clusters fixed; skill document rewritten per rollout.
signatures.selection_rule: Similarity threshold and capacity compaction; no test of whether an entry helps, no retirement by utility, no rollback or versioning.
signatures.persistence: Memory frozen after bootstrapping and injected at test time.
signatures.later_use: At test time the task is routed to its cluster; top-k cosine experiences and the full skill document (adapted per task) are concatenated into the prompt; also injected into 9B/4B models and into other benchmarks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Mean Avg@4 31.40 vs 23.18 (vanilla tools) and 25.87 (XSkill); organizer alone 45.75 vs 39.37 on TIR-Bench; zero-shot transfer to 9B/4B and OOD benchmarks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Cross-type noise in global pool (single case study); on 122B removing the experience cluster costs only 0.12 points.

gap.author_gap: Self-evolving agents (a) spend rollout budget on low-value samples (data inefficiency) and (b) mix heterogeneous knowledge in one global pool (knowledge interference), which interact in a self-reinforcing loop.
gap.checked_gap: Both are plausible, specific shortcomings of prior experience/skill bootstrapping (global pool, uniform traversal), supported by a case study and ablations. The coupling loop and the claim that most prior work uses a single granularity are only partly checked: XSkill, the closest neighbour, already keeps experiences and skills.
gap.lineage: Reflexion -> ExpeL-style experience pools -> XSkill (dual-stream experiences + skills in one global pool) -> Memento-Skills / Trace2Skill / SkillX / SkillRouter; RL-based D2Skill/SkillRL form a separate weight-updating family. Ace-Skill = XSkill-style memory + per-cluster isolation + proficiency-prioritized rollouts.
gap.closest_adjacent: XSkill (compared experimentally on same backbone); SkillRouter (routing over a large registry), D2Skill (dual-granularity skill bank with RL) are named but not compared.
gap.residue: Whether clustering beats other organisations (hierarchy/graph/router) and whether the sampler reduces cost at fixed rollouts; K sensitivity; train/test overlap.
gap.stakes: Rollout/verification cost in long-horizon multimodal tool use and retrieval noise as task diversity grows.
gap.method_response: Prioritized sampler for allocation; clustered dual-granularity organizer for isolation; claimed mutual reinforcement.
gap.remaining_gap: Admission gate and retirement of stored knowledge, independent verifier, open-ended cluster discovery, cost accounting.
unresolved: Neighbour full texts (XSkill, SkillRouter, D2Skill) not fixed in this batch, so gap check relies on the paper's characterisation and Table 2 numbers.

claims.text: Ace-Skill improves Qwen3.5-35B-A3B tool use by +35.46% relative Avg@4 (mean 23.18 -> 31.40) and beats XSkill (25.87) and several proprietary models.
claims.setting: TIR-Bench, VisualToolBench, MMSearch-Plus, AgentVista; Avg@4 and Pass@4; 4 tools.
claims.baseline_control: Vanilla tools (store-off), XSkill (same backbone), proprietary models without bootstrapped knowledge; sourced and reproduced numbers mixed.
claims.selection_vs_test: Split not stated; bootstrapping seems to use each benchmark's own samples; hyperparameters tuned on TIR-Bench.
claims.result: Mean Avg@4 31.40 / Pass@4 48.23 vs 23.18 / 41.32 vanilla and 25.87 / 43.53 XSkill; single run.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On these benchmarks the system with its bootstrapped memory scores higher than the stated baselines (author-reported); generalisation to unseen samples of the same benchmark is not established.

claims.text: The prioritized sampler and clustered organizer each contribute and reinforce each other (super-additively).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Both modules add 6+ points individually and are partly complementary; the combination is sub-additive by the paper's own numbers.

claims.text: Bootstrapped knowledge transfers zero-shot to 9B/4B models and across benchmarks.
claims.baseline_control: Vanilla tools on the same smaller model / target benchmark.
claims.selection_vs_test: OOD pairs are source-disjoint; cross-scale transfer uses the same benchmark samples.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Positive transfer in two source-target pairs and two smaller models in a single run each.

claims.text: The sampler reduces sample complexity/training time vs uniform sampling and inference cost is not higher.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not supported beyond a visitation histogram.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A cluster-isolated, proficiency-prioritized experience/skill memory bootstrapped by Qwen3.5-35B-A3B raises mean Avg@4 on four multimodal tool-use benchmarks over store-off and XSkill baselines (author-reported, single run), and its knowledge improves other benchmarks (two source-target pairs) and smaller models.
assessment.not_supported: That in-domain gains are on unseen samples; the 'super-additive' and 'virtuous cycle' claims; sample-efficiency and inference-cost claims; that clustering is the best organisation.
unresolved: Cluster count K and its sensitivity

G.reason: Two concrete, sourced shortcomings (uniform traversal, global pool) with the nearest neighbour XSkill compared on the same backbone and tools, and a clear residual (cross-type noise, wasted rollouts). Not 4: the coupled 'vicious loop' is asserted, the single-granularity gap is contradicted by XSkill itself, and other organisations/routers are not compared.

M.reason: Operations, inputs and rationale are reproducible: Beta posterior with lazy decay and a three-term priority; cluster-local dual-granularity memory with explicit merge/compress. Predictions that distinguish it from naive alternatives (global pool, uniform sampling) are testable and partly tested. Weak points: heuristic weights, single noisy rollout reward, interaction effect only asserted.

X.reason: Main steps are described and Algorithm 1 is complete, but cluster count K and train/eval protocol are missing, there is no admission gate, utility-based retirement, versioning or rollback, the same model proposes, merges and verifies, and the skill document is rewritten whole each update.

E.measurement.reason: Four established benchmarks with Avg@4 and Pass@4, but scoring/judging procedure is not described in the text, baselines mix sourced and reproduced numbers and different modes (no-thinking Ace-Skill), and the training verifier is the same model family.

E.causality.reason: Store-off, XSkill same-backbone comparison, 2x2 module ablation and component ablations are present. Gaps: ablations on one benchmark only and single run, no budget-matched comparison, no simple context baseline, 'super-additive' contradicted by own numbers, sample-efficiency mechanism unmeasured.

E.holdout.reason: No train/eval split is stated for the headline tables; the bootstrapping pool appears to be each benchmark's own samples and hyperparameters were tuned on TIR-Bench. Only the two source-disjoint OOD pairs provide held-out evidence.

E.statistics.reason: Averages over four attempts and Pass@4 are reported, but no benchmark sizes, seeds, CIs or significance tests; single bootstrapping run per configuration; ablation margins of 1-3 points and 'super-additive' wording unsupported.

E.cost.reason: Bootstrapping budget is given (50 steps, batch 8, 1 rollout per sample, 8xH20 for local models) but no token/time/dollar cost, no matched-budget baseline, and the sample-complexity and inference-cost claims are unquantified.

rationale: XSkill式记忆加聚类隔离与优先采样，TIR等四基准均较无记忆基线和XSkill提升；但未报训练/评测划分、无入库门控、单次运行、超加性说法与数据矛盾。
